Undo the last commit#

Also asked as: uncommit, remove last commit, cancel commit, revert most recent commit, delete last commit, uncommit but keep changes

Keep the work, remove only the commitSafe

git reset --soft HEAD~1

The commit is gone. Your files and staging area are exactly as they were.

Undo git reset --soft HEAD@{1}

Throw away the commit and the work in itDestructive

git reset --hard HEAD~1

Deletes the commit and its changes from your working tree.

Undo git reflog, then git reset --hard <hash> of the lost commit

Already pushed and others may have itSafe

git revert HEAD

Adds a new commit that cancels the last one. History stays intact, nothing breaks for teammates.

Undo git revert the revert commit

See also: undo git add, revert to commit, edit commit message

Unstage a file (undo git add)#

Also asked as: unstage, remove from staging, undo add, remove file from index, unstage a file, git restore --staged, two ways to unstage, remove files from staging area, discard staged changes completely

One fileSafe

git restore --staged <file>

The file leaves the staging area. Your edits stay in the file.

Undo git add <file>

Everything you stagedSafe

git restore --staged .

Legacy form: git reset HEAD

Undo git add .

See also: discard changes, undo last commit

Delete a branch, locally and on the remote#

Also asked as: remove branch, delete local branch, delete remote branch, drop branch, delete branch locally and remotely

Local branch, already mergedSafe

git branch -d <branch>

Refuses if the branch has unmerged commits, which is the protection you want.

Undo git branch <branch> <hash> (find the hash with git reflog)

Local branch, merged or notDestructive

git branch -D <branch>

Deletes even with unmerged commits.

Undo git reflog, then git branch <branch> <hash>, within about 90 days

On the remoteDestructive

git push origin --delete <branch>

Removes the branch for everyone.

Undo git push origin <hash>:refs/heads/<branch> if you still have the commit locally

See also: rename branch, create branch

git pull vs git fetch, the difference#

Also asked as: difference between pull and fetch, what does fetch do, what does pull do, get the latest changes

You want to see what changed before touching your workSafe

git fetch

Downloads new commits from the remote and stops. Your branches and files do not move.

git log HEAD..origin/<branch> --oneline

Shows what came in before you decide to merge it.

Undo Nothing to undo. fetch never touches your work.

You want the remote changes in your branch nowSafe

git pull

fetch plus merge in one step. Use git pull --rebase to replay your local commits on top instead of creating a merge commit.

Undo git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD (only if you had no uncommitted changes)

See also: update branch, reset to remote

Rename a branch#

Also asked as: change branch name, rename local branch, rename remote branch

Local onlySafe

git branch -m <old> <new>

From the branch itself: git branch -m <new>

Undo git branch -m <new> <old>

Already pushedDestructive

git branch -m <old> <new>

Rename locally first.

git push -u origin <new>

Publish the new name and track it.

git push origin --delete <old>

Remove the old name. Tell teammates: they run git fetch --prune.

Undo Repeat the three steps with the names swapped

See also: delete branch, push new branch

Force pull: make my copy exactly match the remote#

Also asked as: force pull, overwrite local files, discard everything local, reset to remote, local changes would be overwritten, commit your changes or stash them before you can merge

Discard local commits and edits on this branchDestructive

git fetch origin

Get the remote state first.

git reset --hard origin/<branch>

Your branch now matches the remote exactly. Local commits and edits to tracked files are gone.

Undo git reflog, then git reset --hard <hash> of your old state

Keep your edits, just in caseDestructive

git stash -u

Saves tracked and untracked changes to the stash first.

git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/<branch>

Recover the saved work later with git stash pop.

Undo git stash pop restores the edits you set aside; local commits need git reflog

See also: stash, remove untracked

Check out a branch that exists on the remote#

Also asked as: switch to remote branch, get remote branch, track remote branch, checkout origin branch, list remote branches

Standard caseSafe

git fetch

Make sure you know about it.

git switch <branch>

Creates a local branch tracking origin/<branch> automatically. Legacy form: git checkout -t origin/<branch>

Undo git switch - returns to your previous branch

See also: clone all branches, create branch

Make Git forget a tracked file that is now in .gitignore#

Also asked as: stop tracking file, remove from repo keep on disk, untrack, remove file from repo but keep it locally, ignore files already committed, remove file from repository without deleting it from disk, remove node_modules from repository, remove directory from remote after gitignore

One fileSafe

git rm --cached <file>

Stops tracking. The file stays on your disk. .gitignore only affects untracked files, which is why ignoring it was not enough.

git commit -m "Stop tracking <file>"

Note: the file is deleted for others when they pull, and it remains in old history.

Undo git add <file> before committing, or git revert afterwards

A whole folderSafe

git rm -r --cached <folder>

Then commit as above.

Undo git add <folder> before committing

See also: ignore files, remove untracked

Delete untracked files from the working tree#

Also asked as: clean untracked, remove new files, git clean, delete files not in repo, delete a single untracked file, reset --hard leaves untracked files, clear my working directory

Always preview firstSafe

git clean -nd

Lists what would be deleted. Nothing happens yet.

Undo Nothing to undo. This only prints.

Actually deleteDestructive

git clean -fd

Deletes untracked files and folders. Add -x to also delete ignored files (build output, .env). There is no reflog for untracked files.

Undo None. This is why you run the preview first.

See also: untrack file, discard changes

Change a commit message#

Also asked as: amend message, fix commit message, reword commit, modify unpushed commit message, change commit message after push, change message of pushed commit

Last commit, not pushedRewrites history

git commit --amend -m "<new message>"

Drop the -m flag to write it in your editor.

Undo git commit --amend -m "<old message>" again

Last commit, already pushedRewrites history

git commit --amend -m "<new message>"
git push --force-with-lease

Rewrites the remote commit. force-with-lease aborts if someone pushed meanwhile, unlike plain --force.

Undo git reflog to find the old commit, then amend back and force-with-lease again

An older commitRewrites history

git rebase -i <hash>^

Change pick to reword on the commit's line, save, write the new message.

Undo git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD right after the rebase

See also: add to last commit, squash commits

Go back to a previous commit#

Also asked as: revert repository, restore old version, rollback, return to earlier commit, time travel, roll back to the previous release

Just look around, change nothingSafe

git switch --detach <hash>

You are viewing the old state. Return with git switch -

Undo git switch -

Undo pushed commits without rewriting historySafe

git revert --no-commit <hash>..HEAD

Stages the exact undo of everything after <hash>.

git commit -m "Revert to <hash>"

One clean commit that returns the project to that state.

Undo git revert that revert commit

Erase everything after a commit, not pushedDestructive

git reset --hard <hash>

The later commits and any uncommitted work are gone from your copy.

Undo git reflog, then git reset --hard <hash> of the state you left

See also: undo last commit, restore file

Change the remote URL#

Also asked as: set-url, switch remote, https to ssh, update origin, change origin url

Point origin somewhere elseSafe

git remote set-url origin <url>

Works for moving between HTTPS and SSH forms of the same repo too.

Undo git remote set-url origin <old-url>

See also: find remote url, upload existing project

Move recent commits to a new branch#

Also asked as: committed to wrong branch, move commits off main, commits on wrong branch

The commits are not pushedDestructive

git branch <new-branch>

The new branch now holds the commits. Your current branch still points at them too.

git reset --hard HEAD~<n>

Move the current branch back n commits. Commit or stash anything uncommitted first.

git switch <new-branch>

Continue working where the commits live.

Undo git reflog on the original branch, then git reset --hard <hash>

See also: cherry pick, undo last commit

Discard uncommitted changes#

Also asked as: throw away changes, undo local edits, restore file to last commit, discard unstaged, revert all local changes, undo all uncommitted changes including new files, revert project to previous state

One fileDestructive

git restore <file>

The file returns to its last committed state.

git checkout -- <file>

The same thing, in the older spelling. Still everywhere in tutorials and in muscle memory.

Undo None. The edits were never committed, so Git has no copy.

Every tracked fileDestructive

git restore .

Untracked files are not touched. Use git clean for those.

Undo None. Stash instead if you are not sure: git stash

See also: stash, remove untracked, undo git add

Reset a branch to exactly match the remote#

Also asked as: local branch same as remote, match origin, sync with remote discard local, reset local branch to remote head, make local identical to origin, reset local branch to be just like remote head, start over completely

Discard local commits on this branchDestructive

git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/<branch>

Add git clean -fd after it if you also want untracked files gone.

Undo git reflog, then git reset --hard <hash> of your old state

See also: overwrite local, update branch

Restore a file from an older commit#

Also asked as: get old version of file, revert single file, file from previous commit, revert file to specific revision, undo changes to one file, checkout file from commit

Bring the old version into your working treeDestructive

git restore --source=<hash> <file>

Overwrites the current file. Legacy form: git checkout <hash> -- <file>

Undo git restore <file> returns to the committed version, but uncommitted edits are lost

Just view it, touch nothingSafe

git show <hash>:<path/to/file>

Prints that version to the terminal. Redirect with > to save a copy.

Undo Nothing to undo

See also: revert to commit, file history

Squash the last N commits into one#

Also asked as: combine commits, merge commits together, clean up commits before pr

No editor, one clean commitRewrites history

git reset --soft HEAD~<n>

The commits vanish; all their changes are staged.

git commit -m "<message>"

One commit now holds the work of n.

Undo git reset --soft HEAD@{2} (check git reflog for the right step)

Pick and choose interactivelyRewrites history

git rebase -i HEAD~<n>

Keep the first line as pick, change the rest to squash or fixup, save.

Undo git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD right after

Already pushedRewrites history

git push --force-with-lease

After either method above. Only on branches where teammates expect rewrites, like your own PR branch.

Undo git reflog locally still has the pre-squash state

See also: edit commit message, undo rebase

Push a new local branch and track it#

Also asked as: publish branch, push branch first time, set upstream, no upstream branch

First push of the branchSafe

git push -u origin <branch>

-u links local and remote so plain git push and git pull work from now on.

Undo git push origin --delete <branch> removes it from the remote

See also: create branch, delete branch

Find where this repository was cloned from#

Also asked as: show remote url, what is origin, remote address, list remotes, what url was this cloned from, show origin url, determine the url the repository was cloned from

Standard caseSafe

git remote -v

Shows every remote with its fetch and push URLs.

Undo Nothing to undo

See also: change remote url

Add an empty directory to the repository#

Also asked as: commit empty folder, keep folder, gitignore vs gitkeep

Standard caseSafe

touch <folder>/.gitkeep

Git tracks files, never directories, so the folder needs one file. .gitkeep is a convention, not a Git feature; any file works.

Undo git rm <folder>/.gitkeep

See also: ignore files

Resolve a merge conflict#

Also asked as: fix conflicts, conflict markers, both modified, merge failed, git merge continue, why do conflicts happen

Work through itSafe

git status

Lists the conflicted files under Unmerged paths.

git diff

Shows the conflicting regions between <<<<<<< and >>>>>>> markers. Edit each file to the final text and delete the markers.

git add <file>

Marks each file resolved.

git commit

Completes the merge. During a rebase, run git rebase --continue instead.

Undo git merge --abort or git rebase --abort at any point before the final step

Take one side wholesale for a fileSafe

git checkout --ours <file>

Keeps your side. Use --theirs for the incoming side. Then git add <file>.

Undo Re-edit the file before git add; nothing is final until the merge commit

See also: undo merge, update branch

Delete a tag, locally and on the remote#

Also asked as: remove tag, delete remote tag, untag

Both placesDestructive

git tag -d <tag>

Local.

git push origin --delete <tag>

Remote. Anyone who fetched the tag keeps it until they delete it too.

Undo git tag <tag> <hash> and push it again

See also: tag release

Undo a merge#

Also asked as: cancel merge, revert merge commit, revert merge after push, undo a merge that has not been pushed, merged too early by accident

Mid-merge, conflicts everywhereSafe

git merge --abort

Returns to the state before the merge started.

Undo Run the merge again

Merged, not pushedDestructive

git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD

ORIG_HEAD is where you stood before the merge. Uncommitted changes are lost.

Undo git reflog, then git reset --hard <hash> of the merge

Merged and pushedSafe

git revert -m 1 <merge-hash>

-m 1 keeps the branch you merged into. History stays intact.

Undo git revert the revert commit

See also: merge conflict, undo rebase

Clone a repository with all branches#

Also asked as: get every branch, clone branches, see remote branches after clone

Standard caseSafe

git clone <url>

This already downloads every branch. They are just not checked out.

git branch -r

Lists them.

git switch <branch>

Creates a local tracking branch for any of them.

See also: checkout remote branch, clone repo

Sync a fork with the original repository#

Also asked as: update fork, fork behind upstream, pull upstream changes, pull original repository into my fork, sync fork button, rebase fork on upstream

From the command lineSafe

git remote add upstream <original-repo-url>

Once per clone. Check with git remote -v.

git fetch upstream
git switch main
git merge upstream/main

Or git rebase upstream/main for a straight-line history.

git push

Your fork on GitHub is now current.

Undo git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD before pushing

One command with GitHub CLISafe

gh repo sync <your-user>/<fork>

GitHub's web UI also has a Sync fork button on the fork's page.

Remove a submodule#

Also asked as: delete submodule, unregister submodule

Standard caseDestructive

git submodule deinit -f <path>

Unregisters it.

git rm -f <path>

Removes the tracked link and the working files.

rm -rf .git/modules/<path>

Clears the leftover internal clone.

git commit -m "Remove submodule <path>"

Undo git revert the commit, then git submodule update --init <path>

Delete a specific commit from a branch#

Also asked as: remove commit from history, drop commit

Not pushedRewrites history

git rebase -i <hash>^

Change pick to drop on the commit's line, save. Later commits are replayed without it; conflicts possible.

Undo git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD right after

Already pushedSafe

git revert <hash>

Adds a commit that cancels it. The honest option on shared branches.

Undo git revert the revert commit

See also: undo last commit, undo rebase

Undo a rebase#

Also asked as: rebase went wrong, revert rebase, recover after rebase, undoing a rebase

Right after it finishedDestructive

git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD

ORIG_HEAD is where the branch stood before the rebase.

Undo git reflog still shows the post-rebase state

Some commands ran sinceDestructive

git reflog

Find the entry just before the line that says rebase (start).

git reset --hard HEAD@{<n>}

Use that entry's number.

Undo The reflog keeps every state for about 90 days; you can move again

See also: squash commits, recover lost commit

Show the current branch name#

Also asked as: what branch am i on, print branch

Standard caseSafe

git branch --show-current

Empty output means detached HEAD: you are on a commit, not a branch.

Undo Nothing to undo

See also: detached head

Fix a detached HEAD#

Also asked as: you are in detached head state, not on a branch, head detached at, reconcile detached head with main, go to a particular revision, keep commits made in detached head

You made no commits hereSafe

git switch <branch>

Back on a branch. Detached HEAD just means you checked out a commit directly; nothing is wrong.

Undo git switch --detach <hash> to go back

You made commits you want to keepSafe

git switch -c <new-branch>

Creates a branch at your current commit. The work is safe and named.

Undo git branch -D <new-branch> discards it again

See also: current branch, recover lost commit

Set work aside temporarily (stash)#

Also asked as: save changes without commit, stash changes, switch branch with uncommitted work, stash pop conflict, stash but keep staged, stash apply vs pop, undo stash pop, stash including ignored files, name a stash, backup before a risky command, drop or clear stashes

Set asideSafe

git stash push -u -m "<label>"

-u includes untracked files, which plain stash silently skips. Your tree is clean now.

Undo git stash pop brings it straight back

Bring backSafe

git stash list

Every stash with its label.

git stash pop

Applies the newest and drops it. git stash apply stash@{<n>} applies a specific one and keeps it in the list.

Undo If pop conflicted, the stash is kept automatically; resolve or git checkout . to retry

See also: discard changes, overwrite local

Also asked as: new branch, make branch, start feature branch, create branch on github website

From where you areSafe

git switch -c <branch>

Legacy form: git checkout -b <branch>

Undo git switch - then git branch -d <branch>

From a specific commit or branchSafe

git switch -c <branch> <start-point>

Undo git switch - then git branch -d <branch>

Clone a repository#

Also asked as: download repo, git clone, copy repository, download code from github, what does cloning mean

Standard caseSafe

git clone <url>

The URL is on the repo page behind the Code button, HTTPS or SSH.

Huge repository, you need it fastSafe

First-time Git setup on a new machine#

Also asked as: configure git, set name and email, git config global, initial setup, git for beginners practical guide

The three settings that matterSafe

git config --global user.name "<your name>"

Goes into every commit you make.

git config --global user.email "<your email>"

Use the same email as your GitHub account so commits link to your profile.

git config --global init.defaultBranch main

New repositories start on main, matching GitHub.

Undo git config --global --unset <key>

See also: upload existing project, clone repo

Also asked as: git log, view commits, history graph, show log, oldest commits first, hide merge commits

Readable one-linersSafe

git log --oneline --graph --all

Every branch as a graph, one line per commit.

Undo Nothing to undo

What each commit changedSafe

git log -p -3

Full diffs for the last three commits. Drop -3 for all.

See what I changed and what is staged#

Also asked as: git diff, git status, show my changes, staged vs unstaged, git diff --cached, see staged changes, diff of file in staging area, diff --stat summary

The overviewSafe

git status

What is staged, what is modified, what is untracked.

The actual editsSafe

git diff

Unstaged edits only.

git diff --staged

See the history of one file#

Also asked as: who changed this file, file log, blame, search history for code

Commits that touched the fileSafe

--follow keeps the trail across renames.

Who last touched each lineSafe

Tag a release and push the tag#

Also asked as: create tag, version tag, annotated tag, push tags, tags not pushed, push commits and tags together

Standard caseSafe

git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "<release note>"

Annotated tags carry author, date, and message. Plain git tag v1.0.0 is a bare pointer.

Also asked as: first push, existing folder to github, init and push, publish project

From the terminalSafe

git push -u origin main

Also asked as: pull latest, update local branch, get new commits

Merge them inSafe

git pull

fetch plus merge. May create a merge commit if you have local commits.

Force push without destroying teammates' work#

Also asked as: force push, push rejected after rebase, force with lease

Always prefer this formRewrites history

git push --force-with-lease

Overwrites the remote branch only if nobody pushed since you last fetched. Plain --force overwrites unconditionally and can erase a teammate's commits.

Undo git reflog has your old branch tip; the remote's old tip is on any machine that fetched it

Recover a lost commit or branch#

Also asked as: deleted branch recover, find lost commit, reflog, accidentally reset, undo git reset

The safety netSafe

git reflog

Every position HEAD has held, with hashes, kept about 90 days. Find the state you lost.

git branch <rescue> <hash>

Names the lost commit so nothing can garbage-collect it. Inspect it with git switch <rescue>.

Undo git branch -D <rescue> if it was not what you wanted

See also: undo rebase, delete branch

Also asked as: gitignore, exclude files, ignore node_modules, ignore env file, gitignore a folder, ignore directory on windows, .gitignore for visual studio, ignoring directories, gitignore file itself shows as untracked, what is gitignore

Standard caseSafe

printf "node_modules/\n.env\ndist/\n" >> .gitignore

One pattern per line. Directories end with /. Patterns match untracked files only.

git rm -r --cached <already-tracked-path>

Only needed for files Git already tracks; then commit.

Undo Delete the line from .gitignore

Start from a proven templateSafe

curl -o .gitignore https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/gitignore/main/Node.gitignore

github/gitignore has maintained templates for every major language. Swap Node for yours.

Undo Delete the file

See also: untrack file, empty directory

Also asked as: move file, git mv, rename keep history, rename a folder, move files and keep history

Generate an SSH key and add it to GitHub#

Also asked as: create ssh key, ssh-keygen, add ssh key to github, ssh setup, ed25519 vs rsa

Generate and registerSafe

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<your email>"

Accept the default path. A passphrase is optional but wise.

cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Copy the output, then paste it at GitHub: Settings, SSH and GPG keys, New SSH key. The same public key works on GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.

Undo Delete the key from the host's settings; remove ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and .pub

ssh -T git@github.com

Success looks like: Hi <username>! You've successfully authenticated.

Undo Nothing to undo

See also: https vs ssh

HTTPS or SSH for remotes, which and why#

Also asked as: https vs ssh github, which remote url, clone with ssh or https

DecidingSafe

git remote set-url origin git@github.com:<user>/<repo>.git

SSH: one key, no token expiry, ideal once set up. Corporate proxies sometimes block port 22.

git remote set-url origin https://github.com/<user>/<repo>.git

HTTPS: works everywhere, authenticates with a token via your credential manager. Passwords alone stopped working in 2021.

Undo set-url back to the other form; the repository itself is identical either way

See also: ssh key github, stop password prompts

Stop Git asking for my password every time#

Also asked as: cache credentials, remember password, credential manager, authentication failed token, save username and password, cache https credentials, git push asks for username and password, clone with username and password, update saved git password, remove credentials from git, git keeps prompting for a password, 403 fatal http request failed

Per operating systemSafe

git config --global credential.helper manager

Windows: Git Credential Manager ships with Git for Windows and signs you in through the browser once.

git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain

macOS: stores the token in your keychain.

git config --global credential.helper "cache --timeout=86400"

Linux: holds it in memory for a day. Git Credential Manager installs on Linux too if you want browser sign-in.

Undo git config --global --unset credential.helper

With GitHub CLISafe

gh auth login

Authenticates git for github.com in one guided step.

Undo gh auth logout

Permanently, with keysSafe

ssh -T git@github.com

If you use SSH remotes there is no password to ask for. See the SSH key answer.

Undo Nothing to undo

See also: ssh key github, https vs ssh

Also asked as: default editor, use vscode for commit, core.editor, change default git editor, use vscode for commit messages

Moves the branch pointer. Rewrites your local history, so it belongs to unpushed work.
